reliable_uses: Defining the minimum Codex skill shape: `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description`, plus optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`, and `agents/openai.yaml`.
Designing progressive disclosure so HSConfig stays discoverable without front-loading HearthRanger syntax into every turn.
Choosing repo-local placement under `.agents/skills` so the skill follows the HSConfig repository instead of the user profile.
Separating instruction-only behavior from deterministic helper scripts and heavier reference material.
Testing trigger quality with explicit and implicit prompts before broadening the skill.
limitations: Official Codex docs define skill packaging and invocation, not HearthRanger or VisionAI config semantics.
Local bundled skills show current patterns and anti-patterns, but they are examples rather than a normative API guarantee.
A lean skill structure alone cannot prove generated `GlobalValues.json`, `Mulligan.json`, or card-local JSON files are strategically correct.
The HSTuner skill demonstrates workflow bloat risk, but it does not establish the only valid operator flow for HSConfig.
architectural_implications: Keep HSConfig as a repo-local skill in `C:\Users\darbo\Documents\HSConfig\.agents\skills\hsconfig` so discovery stays bounded to the repository and its subfolders.
Keep `SKILL.md` short and trigger-oriented: scope, entry conditions, required inputs, output contract, validation command, and hard boundaries.
Move bulky HearthRanger syntax, card-targeting examples, and edge-case notes into `references/` so Codex loads them only when the skill is selected.
Move deterministic work such as deck-code decoding, schema checks, rule normalization, and fixture comparison into `scripts/` so the skill does not narrate mechanical steps.
Keep exactly one representative worked example near the skill, and store richer golden fixtures in repo `tests/fixtures/` rather than expanding `SKILL.md` into a runbook.
Model the skill around one job: produce or revise HSConfig artifacts from cited research inputs; do not bundle post-game tuning, runtime sampling, or patch-apply workflows.
Use `AGENTS.md` for repository-wide guardrails and keep the skill focused on the reusable method; do not duplicate large policy blocks inside the skill.
If broader reuse is later needed across repositories, package the skill as a plugin, but start local first.
recommended_contracts: `input_manifest.json`: deck code, deck name, format, target files, and source citations required for a run.
`research_snapshot.json`: archetype claim, mulligan sources, card-role evidence, and confidence notes that justify generation decisions.
`config_plan.json`: planned surfaces to write (`GlobalValues`, `Mulligan`, `CardID`, `Combo`, optional `Presume` and `Concede`) plus skipped surfaces and reasons.
`generation_result.json`: files written, file hashes, assumptions, unresolved gaps, and `runtime_write_performed=false`.
`validation_report.json`: schema checks, command results, fixture diffs, and pass/fail status for every generated surface.
`example_case.json`: a single minimal worked example used for regression checks of the skill trigger and output shape.
`skill_trigger_eval.csv`: explicit, implicit, and negative prompts used to verify activation boundaries.
never_autogenerate_without: A decoded deck list and authoritative card metadata for every card in the deck.
Cited source material that explains the intended archetype, mulligan priorities, and any non-obvious card behavior used in the config.
A declared output contract that lists exactly which config surfaces may be written in the current run.
A deterministic validation pass over generated JSON files, including syntax, required keys, and repo-specific rule checks.
A reviewable report that records assumptions, skipped surfaces, and any heuristics or guessed values.
At least one golden example or fixture diff showing the generator matches the expected shape for a known deck before wider rollout.
